court: Court of Appeals for the Federal Circuit

issues.label: CFC Tucker Act jurisdiction
issues.why: The court must confirm it has money-mandating jurisdiction over military disability retirement pay claims.

issues.label: Money-mandating source identified
issues.why: The claim must rest on statutes/regulations that mandate pay upon qualifying disability retirement (e.g., Chapter 61).

issues.label: Subject-matter jurisdiction over record correction
issues.why: The court must assess whether DD-214 correction is permissible as incidental equitable relief to a monetary claim.

issues.label: Statute of limitations accrual
issues.why: The court must determine when the 6-year period under 28 U.S.C. § 2501 began to run.

issues.label: Accrual on discharge date
issues.why: A key question is whether the claim accrued at separation when medical retirement was allegedly denied.

issues.label: Accrual on BCNR denial date
issues.why: The court must decide whether accrual instead occurred when the correction board finally denied relief.

issues.label: Accrual-suspension doctrine
issues.why: The court must consider whether accrual was delayed because injury was inherently unknowable or concealed.

issues.label: Equitable tolling unavailable
issues.why: Because § 2501 is jurisdictional, the court must ensure it did not apply impermissible equitable tolling.

issues.label: Effect of voluntary remand
issues.why: The court must determine whether remand/reconsideration affects finality or limitations calculations.

issues.label: Exhaustion/board application requirement
issues.why: The court must decide whether BCNR exhaustion was required or merely permissive for this pay claim.

issues.label: Final agency action identified
issues.why: APA-style review requires a final BCNR decision to review and an administrative record to evaluate.

issues.label: Standard of review correctness
issues.why: The court must apply the highly deferential arbitrary-and-capricious/substantial-evidence standard used for BCNR determinations.

issues.label: Presumption of regularity
issues.why: The court must decide the weight to give the presumption that officials performed duties correctly and lawfully.

issues.label: Burden of proof allocation
issues.why: The court must determine whether the applicant bore the burden to show error/injustice and entitlement to disability retirement.

issues.label: Scope of administrative record
issues.why: The court must decide what materials constitute the record and whether supplementation is allowed.

issues.label: Deference to military judgments
issues.why: Fitness and disability determinations involve military discretion that narrows judicial review.

issues.label: Correct fitness-for-duty standard
issues.why: The court must ensure BCNR applied the legal definition of unfitness under the DES rather than an incorrect proxy.

issues.label: Unfitness vs diagnosis distinction
issues.why: The court must ensure the board did not equate having PTSD/TBI with being unfit, or vice versa.

issues.label: Performance-based fitness evidence
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether continued satisfactory duty, promotion, and instructor service support a fitness finding.

issues.label: Line-of-duty/service connection relevance
issues.why: The court must separate VA service-connection findings from the military unfitness inquiry.

issues.label: VA ratings evidentiary weight
issues.why: The court must decide how much weight to give the VA’s 70%/100% ratings in assessing fitness at discharge.

issues.label: Temporal focus at discharge
issues.why: The legal question is fitness as of April 1, 2013, not later deterioration or later evaluations.

issues.label: Preponderance standard application
issues.why: The court must confirm the board’s use of the correct evidentiary standard for BCNR correction decisions.

issues.label: Requirement to convene MEB/PEB
issues.why: The court must consider whether regulations required referral to the disability evaluation system before VSP separation.

issues.label: Error vs injustice threshold
issues.why: BCNR relief can be based on legal error or injustice; the court must assess whether either was shown.

issues.label: Causation for entitlement to pay
issues.why: Even if there was procedural error, the court must determine whether it would have changed the retirement outcome.

issues.label: Constructive disability retirement
issues.why: The court must decide whether the facts support a deemed/constructive medical retirement remedy.

issues.label: Liberal consideration applicability
issues.why: The court must decide whether 10 U.S.C. § 1552(h) and related policies apply to this PTSD/TBI-based petition.

issues.label: Liberal consideration standard content
issues.why: The court must define what “liberal consideration” requires the board to do when assessing PTSD/TBI evidence.

issues.label: Explicit vs implicit consideration
issues.why: The court must decide whether BCNR had to explicitly state it applied liberal consideration or whether implicit compliance suffices.

issues.label: Compliance with § 1552(h) procedures
issues.why: The court must assess whether statutory requirements (e.g., expertise, review process) for mental health claims were met.

issues.label: Relevant DoD/SECNAV guidance
issues.why: The court must consider binding policy memoranda on PTSD/TBI-related discharge/record correction and their legal effect.

issues.label: Adequacy of BCNR reasoning
issues.why: The decision must show a rational connection between facts found and conclusions, addressing key evidence.

issues.label: Failure to address material evidence
issues.why: The court must evaluate whether BCNR ignored significant medical evidence supporting unfitness.

issues.label: Consideration of combat injury context
issues.why: The court must assess whether the board appropriately weighed combat-related TBI/PTSD circumstances under liberal consideration.

issues.label: Procedural due process fairness
issues.why: The court must consider whether the BCNR process (notice, opportunity to respond, record review) was fundamentally fair.

issues.label: Medical advisory opinions use
issues.why: If advisory opinions were relied on, the court must check their adequacy, qualifications, and whether plaintiff could rebut them.

issues.label: Fitness presumption from active duty
issues.why: The court must consider the regulatory presumption that continued duty may indicate fitness and when it can be rebutted.

issues.label: Effect of VSP voluntary separation
issues.why: The court must determine whether voluntary VSP separation affects eligibility for disability retirement or DES processing duties.

issues.label: Narrative reason correction standard
issues.why: The court must decide the legal criteria for changing DD-214 narrative reason versus granting disability retirement status.

issues.label: Remedy scope and calculation
issues.why: If plaintiff prevails, the court must determine proper relief: retired pay amount, effective date, and ancillary corrections.

issues.label: Offset/recoupment considerations
issues.why: The court must consider how VA compensation interacts with military retired pay (offsets/waivers) in computing monetary relief.

issues.label: Combat-related special compensation
issues.why: The court must consider whether CRSC/other statutory benefits are implicated by a disability retirement determination.

issues.label: Interest and back pay limits
issues.why: The court must apply statutory limits on interest and any restrictions on back pay against the United States.

issues.label: Attorney fees eligibility
issues.why: The court must consider potential EAJA eligibility depending on prevailing party status and substantial justification.

issues.label: Harmless error doctrine
issues.why: Even if the board used imperfect wording, the court must decide whether any error was prejudicial.

issues.label: Review of CFC merits disposition
issues.why: The court must assess whether granting judgment on the administrative record was proper under RCFC 52.1 standards.

issues.label: Standard for remand vs reversal
issues.why: If error is found, the court must decide whether to remand to BCNR for reconsideration or order correction/retirement directly.
